title: Path Diffuser: Diffusion Model for Data-Driven Traffic Simulator

control_signal.value: Vectorized map for initialization; per-agent initial pose and attributes plus Frenet-frame candidate trajectories as motion-primitive priors for trajectory generation. No user-specified behaviour goals in packet.

control_mechanism.value: Map-conditioned DDPM for initialization; noisy latent trajectories cross-attend to Frenet candidates in heterogeneous message passing; guided sampling aligns predictions to the nearest candidate under map perturbation.

base_model.value: Two-stage diffusion: differential-transformer initializer with centralized/decentralized attention masking; trajectory denoiser on PCA-compressed latent trajectories with alternating cross- and self-attention over agents and map.

datasets.value: Argoverse 2 Motion Forecasting Dataset, 6-second windows; Scene-Attack benchmark used for out-of-distribution map perturbations.

metrics.value: JSD of behaviour histograms, collision rate, nearest-edge distance, off-road rate; actor collision rate, lateral deviations; FDE, ADE, miss rate.

controllability_evidence.value: Abstract reports 1.92× on distribution metrics, 1.14× on common-sense metrics, 1.62× on road compliance. Initialization collision rate 6.09% for PD versus 17.16% for MHA baseline. No steering experiment in packet.

stated_limitations.value: Fixed 6-second horizon from PCA; about 10 hours training; two separate models are costly; closed-loop evaluation not yet done; Frenet candidate grid predefined; no richer context such as signals or weather.

notes: Not really a controllable-generation paper: controllability is limited to map and initial-state conditioning; test-time controllability is listed as future work. Conclusion mentions improved 'scene controllability' only loosely.
